c.tagline: Charlemagne's cathedral capital on Germany's tri-border corner with Belgium and the Netherlands.

taxi.fareNote: German taxis are legally required to run on the meter (Taxameter); flat rates are only common for pre-booked airport transfers.

emergency.note: 112 is the EU-wide number connecting to ambulance and fire services and works from any mobile phone, even without a SIM card.

english.label: Easy to get by in English

avoid.reason: Keep an eye on belongings around the Hauptbahnhof and bus station late at night and in Christmas-market crowds, where pickpockets work.

hood_desc: The compact medieval core around Aachen Cathedral, the Rathaus and Elisenbrunnen, packed with cafes, shops and museums; best for first-time visitors who want everything walkable.

A former independent spa town now part of Aachen, built around thermal springs, abbey buildings and the Kurpark; suits travelers wanting a quieter, wellness-oriented stay a short tram ride from the center.
A lively student quarter near the Ponttor gate and RWTH Aachen University, full of bars, kebab shops and late-night energy; suits younger travelers wanting nightlife.
The area around Aachen Hauptbahnhof and the Marschiertor gate, convenient for arrivals with chain hotels and easy tram/bus connections to the rest of the city.
A leafy residential district around the medieval Burg Frankenberg castle, appealing to families and those wanting a calmer, greener base a short walk from downtown.

water.note: Tap water is excellent quality and safe to drink everywhere.

transit.hours: Buses run roughly 5:00 AM to 1:00 AM, with a reduced weekend night-bus network filling in after midnight.
transit.pay: Tickets are bought from the driver, ticket machines, or the AVV/ASEAG app (eTicket); a regional day pass covers buses and trains across the Aachen area.
transit.note: Aachen has no tram or subway; ASEAG buses are the backbone of city transit, supplemented by regional trains at Aachen Hauptbahnhof for trips to Cologne, Liège and Maastricht.

train: International connections to Liège, Brussels and Paris
Regional trains (RE/RB) to Cologne, Düsseldorf, Liège and Maastricht

car.idp: Not required for EU/US licenses; recommended for others

transit.m: Train via Köln Hauptbahnhof to Aachen Hauptbahnhof (~70-90 min total)

tip.r: Rounding up the bill or adding roughly 5-10% for good service is customary, even though a service charge is already included in the price by law.
